payload.task_text:
Your research institution must establish comprehensive data archival and compliance procedures to ensure research data integrity and meets regulatory requirements. The first phase involves conducting a complete inventory of all research datasets and associated documentation. Identify all active research projects and their data files. Document dataset characteristics including file format, size, creation date, and data type. Organize documentation including study protocols, data collection procedures, and analytical methods. Create a centralized registry of all research datasets with essential metadata for each.

In the second phase, you will verify compliance of all datasets with applicable retention policies and funding agency requirements. Review institutional data retention policies specifying how long different data types must be retained. Check funding agency requirements including National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, and other sponsor mandates. Assess whether datasets meet funder requirements for data sharing and open access. Document any datasets with sensitive data requiring restricted access or deidentification. Verify that datasets include required documentation and metadata for reproducibility.

The third phase requires creating comprehensive archival metadata and preservation plans for each dataset. Develop standardized metadata documentation following relevant community standards for the research domain. Create detailed data dictionaries defining all variables and coding schemes. Document data provenance including collection methods, preprocessing steps, and quality assurance procedures. Create preservation plans addressing long-term storage, format migration, and access preservation for each dataset.

In the fourth phase, you will organize all research data in a compliant repository structure. Establish standardized directory hierarchies and naming conventions for all datasets. Ensure all files are in acceptable formats suitable for long-term preservation. Create backup copies of all datasets with off-site replication. Establish access controls ensuring appropriate security for sensitive data. Document all datasets in the institutional research data management system.

The fifth phase involves generating comprehensive compliance documentation. Create detailed archival plans for each dataset documenting retention requirements and preservation procedures. Verify that all documentation required by funders is complete and properly organized. Generate compliance checklists for each funding source. Create institutional compliance certifications confirming that data meets all applicable requirements.

The sixth phase requires finalizing archival and communicating with stakeholders. Document all archival procedures and create training materials for researchers. Send compliance verification communications to institutional leadership and funding agencies. Store all archival documentation with version control in the institutional repository. Schedule meetings with research teams to confirm data organization and compliance with requirements.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. The three task-provided datasets are small enough to inventory directly: in one native-parallel read-only batch, inspect these exact task-visible source objects — raw_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/{metadata.json,temperature_records.csv,study_protocol.txt}, raw_datasets/NIH-2022-HLTH-002/{metadata.json,patient_outcomes.csv,study_protocol.txt}, and raw_datasets/DOE-2023-ENRG-003/{metadata.json,measurements.csv,study_protocol.txt}. For each dataset freeze its exact project key, funder, PI, retention years, sensitivity, data file format/size/header/row count, protocol coverage, variable dictionary, provenance evidence, sharing/access constraints, documentation gaps, and preservation risks; treat unrelated top-level sample/config files as workspace context, not research datasets, and preserve every source unchanged. Then directly: create one explicit directory per frozen dataset with preservation copies of every mapped data/documentation file (originals untouched, workspace-only backups labeled as local simulations, and an off-site capability blocker recorded unless an authorized remote target is actually visible) plus the centralized dataset registry; create the compliance documentation package (archival plan, data dictionary, provenance/preservation/access procedure, sponsor checklist, researcher training guidance, version-control instructions, and a certification separating verified compliance from gaps) for every dataset and sponsor. Reconcile the three dataset keys across registry, copies and documents; resolve email recipients and meeting dates/times only from task-visible evidence, reporting the precise missing-parameter blocker instead of guessing, and complete the remaining side effects exactly once. Call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are a coder sub-agent. Create the Phase 5.1 archival plan document for research project NSF-2021-CLIM-001.

Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

CONTEXT — read these existing artifacts to inform your document (READ-ONLY; do not modify them):
- archived_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/metadata/dataset_metadata.json (standardized metadata: funder, retentionYears, sensitive, accessRights, PI, title)
- archived_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/preservation/preservation_plan.md (preservation procedures)
- archived_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/README.md (landing page facts)
- compliance/retention_policy.md (retention tiers)
- compliance/funder_requirements.md (funder-specific requirements for NSF / NIH / DOE)
- compliance/sensitive_data_assessment.md (sensitive data findings)

DELIVERABLE: Create `archived_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/compliance/archival_plan.md` — a detailed archival plan with ALL of these sections:

## 1. Dataset Identification — project ID, title, PI, funder, retention (years), sensitive flag, access status.
## 2. Retention Requirements — institutional retention tier (T1/T2/T3) and period; disposition eligibility year (= project start year + retention years: NSF-2021-CLIM-001 → 2028, NIH-2022-HLTH-002 → 2032, DOE-2023-ENRG-003 → 2028); funder minimums met (NSF ≥3yr, NIH ≥3yr, DOE ≥3yr).
## 3. Preservation Procedures — summarize the preservation plan: storage locations (institutional repo + off-site backup paths), format (CSV/UTF-8), migration strategy, integrity monitoring (checksums.sha256 path), review schedule.
## 4. Sensitive Data Handling — for NIH-2022-HLTH-002: restricted access (restricted/ dir, mode 600), de-identified open copy path, IRB/DUA requirements. For others: state no sensitive data.
## 5. Funder Compliance — which funder requirements apply (from funder_requirements.md) and how this dataset satisfies them (DMP, data sharing/open access, repository deposit).
## 6. Required Documentation Checklist — the documentation that must accompany the dataset (protocol, metadata.json, dataset_metadata.json, data_dictionary.csv, provenance.json, preservation_plan.md, this archival plan) with file paths; mark each as present.
## 7. Access & Sharing — access status (open/restricted), license/rights.
## 8. Review & Versioning — review cadence and version control note (changes tracked in documentation/version_control_log.md).
## 9. Disposition — what happens after retention period per institutional policy.

VERIFICATION: after writing, re-read the file and confirm all 9 sections are present; report the file path and the disposition year used. Do NOT modify any other files (especially not the Phase 3 metadata/preservation artifacts or raw_datasets/).

You are a coder sub-agent. Create the Phase 6 archival procedures documentation and researcher training materials for a research data archival & compliance program.

Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

CONTEXT — the program is already executed; the workspace contains (verify with read-only file listing):
- registry/ (dataset_registry.csv, dataset_registry.json, inventory_report.md) — Phase 1 inventory
- compliance/ (retention_policy.md, funder_requirements.md, sensitive_data_assessment.md, compliance_matrix.csv, compliance_checklists/{NSF,NIH,DOE}_checklist.md, certifications/institutional_compliance_certification.md + .docx) — Phases 2 & 5
- archived_datasets/<PROJECT>/ for NSF-2021-CLIM-001, NIH-2022-HLTH-002, DOE-2023-ENRG-003, each with data/, docs/, metadata/ (dataset_metadata.json, data_dictionary.csv, provenance.json), preservation/ (preservation_plan.md, checksums.sha256), compliance/ (archival_plan.md), README.md — Phases 3 & 4
- offsite_backup/ (mirror of archived_datasets) and checksums/aggregate.sha256 — Phase 4
- NIH-2022-HLTH-002 has restricted/ (raw PHI file mode 600 + README) and data/patient_outcomes_deidentified.csv

DELIVERABLES — create exactly these two files:

1. `documentation/archival_procedures.md` — a procedures manual titled "# Research Data Archival Procedures" documenting the complete archival workflow so staff can repeat it for future datasets. Include sections:
   ## 1. Purpose and Scope
   ## 2. Roles and Responsibilities (Office of Research Compliance, Data Governance Committee, PIs/researchers, IT)
   ## 3. Archival Workflow (step-by-step procedures mapped to the six phases: 3.1 Inventory & Registration; 3.2 Compliance Verification; 3.3 Metadata & Preservation Planning; 3.4 Repository Organization & Backup; 3.5 Compliance Documentation; 3.6 Finalization & Communication)
   ## 4. Standards and Conventions (directory structure, naming conventions — project IDs like <FUNDER>-<YEAR>-<TOPIC>-<NNN>, file formats CSV/UTF-8, metadata standard DataCite 4.4/Dublin Core)
   ## 5. Sensitive Data Handling Procedure (identification, restricted storage, de-identification, access control, DUA/IRB)
   ## 6. Backup and Integrity Procedures (off-site replication, SHA-256 checksums, verification cadence)
   ## 7. Retention and Disposition Procedures
   ## 8. Documentation and Version Control (version_control_log.md)
   ## 9. References (paths to all compliance documents)

2. `documentation/training_materials.md` — researcher training guide titled "# Research Data Archival & Compliance — Training Materials for Researchers" including:
   ## 1. Why Data Archival Compliance Matters
   ## 2. Researcher Responsibilities
   ## 3. What to Submit (data files, study protocol, metadata; naming conventions)
   ## 4. How to Handle Sensitive Data (PHI: restricted access, de-identification)
   ## 5. Metadata and Data Dictionaries: How to Document Your Data (with the example of the three datasets)
   ## 6. Preservation and Retention Basics (retention tiers T1=10yr, T2=7yr, T3=5yr; format migration)
   ## 7. Access to the Institutional Registry and Repository (registry/, archived_datasets/)
   ## 8. Frequently Asked Questions (5-8 Q&As)
   ## 9. Contacts and Resources

Both documents must reference the real artifact paths (e.g., compliance/retention_policy.md, registry/dataset_registry.csv, archived_datasets/...) and use the real project names. Keep content professional and complete (each file should be substantial — target 80+ lines each).

VERIFICATION: after writing, re-read both files, confirm all sections exist, and report the two file paths. Do NOT modify any other files.
